nodes.description: Multi-agent adjuvant cytotoxic chemotherapy (cisplatin, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, and lomustine) achieves high cure rates in WNT-activated medulloblastoma—thought to be aided by fenestrated tumor vasculature lacking an intact blood-brain barrier—with cumulative alkylator (cyclophosphamide) exposure acting as a key determinant preventing metastatic relapse during therapy de-escalation.

evidence.reference_title: Pattern of Relapse and Treatment Response in WNT-Activated Medulloblastoma.

evidence.reference_title: Evolving Biology and Therapy of WNT-Activated Medulloblastoma.
evidence.snippet: The vasculature of WNT-activated medulloblastoma is thought to contribute to these favorable outcomes, as it mimics peripheral vascular endothelium, functionally eliminating the blood-brain barrier and increasing tumor susceptibility to systemic therapies.

nodes.description: Postoperative craniospinal irradiation (CSI) with posterior-fossa/tumor-bed boost controls microscopic leptomeningeal and local residual disease; because 5-year survival exceeds 90%, prospective clinical trials in low-risk M0 WNT-activated disease evaluate reduced-dose CSI (typically 15-18 Gy vs standard 23.4 Gy, while preserving craniospinal coverage) to reduce neurocognitive and endocrine late effects.

evidence.reference_title: Evolving Biology and Therapy of WNT-Activated Medulloblastoma.
evidence.snippet: With 5-year progression-free and overall survival exceeding 90% for WNT-activated medulloblastoma, and given the significant morbidity and late effects of current treatments, several trials are evaluating de-escalation of both craniospinal radiotherapy and adjuvant chemotherapy.
